question: A 230 V source is connected to a 46 ohm resistor. Calculate the current.
Two discrete-time signals are x[n] = [1, 5, 3] and h[n] = [1, 2]. Calculate the convolution output of these two signals at index n = 2.
An RC low-pass filter has a resistance of 1000 ohms and a capacitance of 1 microfarad. Calculate its cutoff frequency in Hz.
A four-point discrete Fourier transform is applied to the sequence x[n] = [5, 2, 7, 3]. Calculate the magnitude of the DC component X[0].
A sinusoidal signal with a frequency of 7000 Hz is sampled at 8000 samples per second. Calculate its aliased frequency in the Nyquist frequency range.

An ideal 12-bit ADC has a full-scale input range from -2.5 V to +2.5 V. Its quantization noise is assumed to be uniformly distributed. The signal is a full-scale sinusoid. The ADC output is oversampled by a factor of 16, followed by ideal low-pass filtering and decimation. Assuming white quantization noise and no other noise sources, calculate the resulting in-band signal-to-quantization-noise ratio (SQNR) in dB.
An FIR filter has the impulse response h[n] = [6, 12, 11]. Calculate the magnitude of its frequency response at the digital angular frequency omega = pi/2 radians per sample.

An input signal x[n] = [1, 3, 2, 5] passes through two cascaded FIR filters with impulse responses h1[n] = [3, 1, 2] and h2[n] = [1, -1]. Assuming zero initial conditions and zero-based indexing, calculate the output sample y[4] of the complete cascaded system.

A digital IIR filter is described by the difference equation y[n] = 0.5y[n-1] + 0.25x[n] + 0.25x[n-1]. The initial conditions are y[-1] = 0 and x[-1] = 0. The input sequence is x[0] = 2, x[1] = 0, x[2] = 2, and x[3] = 0. Calculate the output sample y[3].

A single-phase transformer has 1000 turns in its primary winding and 200 turns in its secondary winding. If the primary voltage is 230 V, calculate the secondary voltage, assuming an ideal transformer.

An ideal single-phase transformer has 800 turns in its primary winding and 200 turns in its secondary winding. The secondary winding supplies a load drawing 40 A. Calculate the current in the primary winding.

A single-phase transformer is connected to a 240 V RMS AC source. The primary winding draws 4 A at a lagging power factor of 0.75. The secondary winding supplies a load with impedance Z = 40 + j30 ohms, and the secondary terminal voltage is 200 V RMS. Calculate the transformer efficiency as a percentage using the active input and output powers.

A transformer has 500 primary turns and operates at 50 Hz. If the applied primary voltage is 230 V RMS, calculate the maximum magnetic flux in the core, assuming sinusoidal excitation and negligible primary winding voltage drop.

A three-phase transformer has a rated power of 100 kVA and a rated secondary line-to-line voltage of 400 V. Its percentage impedance is 5% on its own rated base. Calculate the RMS three-phase symmetrical short-circuit line current at the secondary terminals when the rated primary voltage is applied. Assume the upstream source impedance is negligible.
A transformer has a no-load secondary voltage of 240 V and a full-load secondary voltage of 228 V. Calculate its voltage regulation using the no-load voltage as the reference.

Two transformers operate in parallel and supply a total load of 800 kVA. Transformer A has a rated capacity of 500 kVA and an impedance of 5%. Transformer B has a rated capacity of 1000 kVA and an impedance of 4%. Assume identical voltage ratios, phase displacement, and compatible impedance characteristics. Calculate the apparent power supplied by Transformer A in VA.

A transformer has an equivalent resistance of 0.08 ohms and an equivalent reactance of 0.15 ohms, both referred to the secondary side. The secondary current is 100 A at a lagging power factor of 0.8. Calculate the approximate secondary voltage drop using the first-order transformer voltage regulation approximation, considering only the in-phase component of the impedance voltage drop.

A three-phase transformer operates at 11 kV on the primary side and 400 V on the secondary side. It supplies a balanced load drawing 1200 A at a power factor of 0.85. Calculate the active output power in watts, assuming negligible losses.

A 200 kVA transformer has a constant core loss of 1.2 kW and a full-load copper loss of 2.8 kW. Calculate the fraction of rated load at which maximum efficiency occurs, assuming constant voltage and power factor.
A control system has the transfer function G(s) = 6/(3s + 1). What is its DC gain?
A first-order control system has the transfer function G(s) = 5/(0.25s + 1). What is its time constant?
An underdamped standard second-order control system has a unit-step maximum overshoot ratio of 0.20 and a damped oscillation period of 0.5 seconds. Calculate its damping coefficient.
A first-order control system has the transfer function G(s) = 4/(0.5s + 1). A unit step input is applied at time zero. Calculate the system output at t = 0.25 seconds.
A standard second-order control system has a damping ratio of 0.5. Find the maximum overshoot ratio of the system for a unit step input.
A unity-feedback control system has an open-loop transfer function G(s) = 20/[s(s + 4)]. A ramp input defined by r(t) = 2t is applied. Calculate the steady-state tracking error.

An ideal parallel-form PID controller has proportional gain Kp = 2, integral gain Ki = 0.5, and derivative gain Kd = 0.1. The error signal is e(t) = 2 + 3t for t >= 0. The integral term is initially zero. Calculate the controller output at t = 2 seconds using the control law formula.

A control system has an open-loop transfer function G(s) = K/[s(s + 2)(s + 5)] and uses unity negative feedback. Calculate the positive gain K at which the closed-loop system reaches the boundary of stability.

A plant has the transfer function G(s) = 1/[s(s + 2)] and is controlled using an ideal parallel-form PID controller C(s) = Kp + Ki/s + Kd*s. The system uses unity negative feedback. The closed-loop poles are located at s = -1, s = -2, and s = -3. Calculate the sum of Kp, Ki and Kd that achieves these poles.

A control system has an open-loop transfer function G(s) = 10/(s + 2) and uses unity negative feedback. A sinusoidal reference input with an amplitude of 3 and an angular frequency of 4 rad/s is applied. Calculate the steady-state amplitude of the system output.
